newsitem.title: USA: US Airways files for offering of BA stock.
newsitem.headline: US Airways files for offering of BA stock.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc said Monday it filed for a public offering of convertible preferred stock held by an affiliate of British Airways Plc.
Upon completion of the proposed offering, the turbulent relationship between US Airways and BA would come to an end.
BA said it December it planned to sell its 24.6 percent stake in its estranged marketing partner. In February, US Airways said it would not exercise its right to buy back BA's stake.

British Airways invested about $400 million in US Airways in 1993. While US Airways said the proposed offering still has a "face value" of about $400, the filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission indicates the proposed maximum offering price is $531 million.
US Airways said the proposed offering consistes of about 40,000 Series F, T-1 and T-2 shares. The shares will be offered as depositary shares representing fractional interests in the preferred stock.
Arlington, Va.-based US Airways said it will not receive any of the proceeds of the offering and the sale of the stock will be carried out by British Airways.
US Airways and BA began feuding publicly last summer after BA proposed a broad alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines.

US Airways sued BA in July, alleging the proposed BA- American deal undermined the existing relationship between US Airways and BA. US Airways also contended the proposed deal would allow BA and American to monopolize air travel between the United States and Britain.
Three of BA's directors resigned from US Airways's board in January as the two carriers continued to dismantle their contentious relationship.
